Arbe launches Gryphon 4D radar for unmanned ground vehicles

The system uses 48 transmit and 48 receive channels to support perception on rough terrain and in degraded visibility.

PR Newswire ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Radar for off-road autonomy

Arbe Robotics introduced Gryphon on October 19 as a 4D imaging radar for unmanned ground vehicles operating through dust, rough terrain and unpaved routes. The company targets logistics, mining, agriculture, industrial and defense applications.

Data for obstacles and navigable space

Its 48 transmit and 48 receive channels generate a dense point cloud. Arbe says the data can separate rocks, debris, vegetation and other obstacles, including holes or washed-out ground, while supporting free-space mapping, tracking, odometry and localization where GNSS is unavailable.

A sensor still needs vehicle-level validation

Gryphon uses solid-state hardware without moving parts and is designed for platforms from small vehicles to heavy machinery. These are manufacturer descriptions; the release does not provide independent field comparisons, pricing or delivery dates. A radar launch does not certify the safety of an entire autonomous vehicle in every condition.
